source_name: Fitch Ratings - Hungarian bank rating action commentaries (Erste Bank Hungary, K&H, CIB, MFB, Eximbank)
source_subtype: credit rating agency rating action commentary
why_relevant: Fitch is the main agency covering the foreign-owned Hungarian subsidiaries (Erste Bank Hungary, K&H/KBC, CIB/Intesa) and the state policy banks. Its Rating Action Commentaries are the only public per-entity analytical text for several of these, which publish no standalone English annual report.

source_name: ESMA European Rating Platform (ERP)
why_relevant: Regulator-run free database of every rating and outlook issued by ESMA-registered/certified CRAs (excluding investor-pays), daily updated, history from 1 July 2015, with accompanying press releases. This is the legally clean, licence-free spine for tracking all rating actions on Hungarian banks across Moody's/S&P/Fitch/Scope without touching agency paywalls.

source_name: Céginformációs Szolgálat - beszámoló állomány értékesítése (bulk accounts dataset sale)
why_relevant: Official channel to license the full filed-accounts corpus in bulk rather than scraping e-beszamolo one company at a time - the legally clean path to systematic auditor-opinion coverage across all Hungarian credit and payment institutions.

source_name: Könyvvizsgálói Közfelügyeleti Hatóság (Audit Public Oversight Authority, NGM) - quality-control plans and annual reports
why_relevant: The state audit oversight body publishes annual reports and yearly quality-inspection plans covering audits of public-interest entities (banks, insurers). Reveals which Big4/other firms audit PIEs, inspection findings and deficiency themes - a quality signal on the audit opinions attached to bank accounts.

source_name: Magyar Könyvvizsgálói Kamara (MKVK) - chamber register, transparency-report rules and committee communiqués
why_relevant: Chamber of Hungarian Auditors: registry of audit firms and members, and the legal framework requiring audit firms serving public-interest entities to publish an annual atlathatosagi jelentes (transparency report) on their own websites within 3 months of year-end. Pointer to per-firm transparency reports and to who may audit banks.

source_name: MKVK Oktatási Központ (MKVKOK) - sector guidance 'Hitelintézetek beszámolójának elemzése'
why_relevant: Professional-training material explaining how Hungarian credit-institution statutory accounts are structured and audited. Methodology source: tells the collector what line items and audit judgements to expect in filed bank accounts, and the correct Hungarian terminology for parsing them.

source_name: Deloitte Magyarország - CE Banking Outlook / 'Bank ma' Hungarian banking market study
why_relevant: Deloitte's CE Banking Outlook aggregates per-bank data across 8 CE countries including Hungary with methodology attached, and the Hungarian 'Bank ma' study plus the annual M&A Tranzakcios kitekinto quantify consolidation (bank count halving in 10 years, 3 HU banking transactions in each of 2024 and 2025, MBH most active). Big4 sector aggregation with named sourcing.

source_name: KPMG Magyarország - tanulmányok (studies) hub incl. Banking CEO Outlook and Vállalathitelezési Hangulatindex
why_relevant: KPMG HU runs recurring primary surveys of Hungarian bank executives: the Vallalathitelezesi Hangulatindex (corporate lending sentiment index, built from lending heads' assessments of appetite, conditions and sector attractiveness) and the localised Banking CEO Outlook. Survey instruments with disclosed methodology - rare structured sentiment data on HU lending.

source_name: KPMG Blog Hungary (blog.kpmg.hu) - banking sector commentary
why_relevant: KPMG Hungary publishes the readable digest of its own surveys here (e.g. Dec-2025 post on banking-sector profit/cost expectations after AI adoption, citing that half of bank leaders expect >=2.5% growth). Faster and less gated than the formal study PDFs, and useful for detecting that a new survey exists.

source_name: PwC Magyarország - pénzügyi szektor hub and publication store
source_subtype: Big4 sector survey and publication store
why_relevant: PwC HU runs the Magyarorszagi Penzugyi Vezetoi Felmeres (Hungarian CFO/finance-leader survey, 5th edition, 100+ finance leaders interviewed) and the Digitalis Penzugyi Korkep on digital payment behaviour - directly on-topic for payments as well as banking. Publications are indexed on store.pwc.hu.

source_name: Világgazdaság (vg.hu) and Tőzsdefórum - rating-action reporting on Hungarian banks
why_relevant: Secondary Hungarian business press that reports agency decisions with the detailed rating stack (deposit ratings, BCA, subordinated notches) restated in Hungarian - useful redundancy when Portfolio is paywalled and for the exact Hungarian rating vocabulary.

source_name: Erste Group Bank AG - Ratings page (parent-level disclosure covering Erste Bank Hungary)
why_relevant: Foreign-owned Hungarian subsidiaries (Erste Bank Hungary, K&H/KBC, CIB/Intesa, Raiffeisen, UniCredit) are rated largely on parent support; the parent IR ratings pages carry the agency assessments and support assumptions that determine the Hungarian unit's rating. Access route when the subsidiary itself discloses nothing.

source_name: S&P Global Market Intelligence - European bank rankings and Hungarian bank coverage
why_relevant: Separate from the ratings arm: SPGMI publishes ranked, methodology-documented comparisons of European banks (its inaugural European Bank Ranking put OTP first) and news pieces restating HU rating changes. Aggregated per-bank financial metrics with disclosed methodology.

source_name: TheBanks.eu - Major Banks of Hungary (third-party bank register with rating fields)
why_relevant: Compact aggregator listing Hungarian banks by total assets/market share alongside which agency rates each entity and at what level (e.g. MBH Baa2 Moody's / NR Fitch). Useful as the seed entity list telling the collector which banks are rated by whom, and which are rated by nobody.

source_name: Budapest Business Journal - ratings section (English-language HU rating coverage)
why_relevant: Dedicated English-language 'ratings' vertical covering Hungarian sovereign and bank rating actions - the accessible English bridge for actions first announced in Hungarian, and a de facto index of when rating events happened.

source_name: OTP Bank IR – Elemzők és elemzői konszenzus (analysts & analyst consensus)
why_relevant: Issuer-maintained list of ~20 covering brokerages (Concorde, Erste Group, Wood & Company, Patria, IPOPEMA, mBank, Pekao, PKO BP, Trigon, Autonomous, Citi, Morgan Stanley, BofA, Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, HSBC, UBS, ODDO BHF, Römer Capital) PLUS downloadable quarterly and annual analyst consensus files back to Q1 2023. This is the single best enumerable map of who produces sell-side output on the Hungarian banking sector, and the consensus PDFs give dated expectation series without needing paid research.

source_name: Concorde Értékpapír Zrt. – Research / Elemzés
why_relevant: Concorde is the most-quoted domestic sell-side house on Hungarian banks (OTP, MBH, 4iG, AutoWallis); its research desk publishes quarterly fundamental notes on the largest regional companies and its OTP target-price revisions are the reference domestic anchor. Head of research (Bukta Gábor) is routinely quoted post-earnings, which surfaces the reasoning even when the note itself is client-only.

source_name: Erste Market – Elemzések (Erste Befektetési Zrt. research portal)
why_relevant: Erste Befektetési Zrt. is the largest retail-facing Hungarian broker research shop; publishes company analyses, technical analyses and macro notes largely free-to-web, and covers Hungarian banks and the payments/fintech-adjacent listed names.

source_name: Erste Market – Elemzői ajánlásaink összesítése (recommendation track record)
why_relevant: A cumulative, dated register of Erste's open and closed recommendations since May 2017 — a rare public longitudinal series of a Hungarian broker's calls, usable to reconstruct sentiment history on bank stocks rather than just the current view.

source_name: OTP Global Markets – hírek és elemzések (multi-asset research desk)
why_relevant: Since 2022 the OTP Global Markets Directorate's Multi-asset Analysis Department carries equity-research duties for the group; it publishes dated market/technical/company notes free to web. Note the conflict: OTP's own desk also covers peers, so its bank-sector notes are informative but not independent.

source_name: OTP Elemzési Központ (OTP Analysis Centre) incl. Heti naptár
why_relevant: Macro/banking-market forecasting unit covering Hungary and OTP Group countries, with a named analyst roster and a weekly calendar ('Heti naptár') of data releases and events — the calendar is a scheduling backbone for anticipating when disclosure/earnings flow arrives.

source_name: BÉT – Események (Kibocsátói Fórum / Befektetői Klub / issuer-investor events)
why_relevant: The exchange organises the issuer-facing 'Kibocsátói Fórum' and the retail-facing 'Befektetői Klub'; agendas, speaker lists and slide decks are dated and public, and forum sessions cover disclosure-rule changes and sustainability reporting at listed companies — i.e. forward notice of what issuers will have to publish.

source_name: BÉT Xmatch (closed-round issuer–investor matchmaking events + betxmatch.hu platform)
source_subtype: exchange matchmaking event programme (partly closed platform)
why_relevant: Launched Nov 2019, Xmatch puts capital-seeking companies in front of Hungarian institutional investors and capital-market intermediaries with live Q&A; the 2021 betxmatch.hu platform is a closed matching venue. Event announcements reveal which fintech/payments-adjacent companies are seeking capital before any public filing exists — an early-warning indirect signal.

source_name: BÉT / BSE press room – Sajtóközlemények (press releases)
why_relevant: The exchange's own press feed is where investor-event editions, new listings, Xtend admissions and programme launches are announced first; it is the pointer that keeps the event and issuer actor-map current.

source_name: BÉT E-Akadémia – Prezentációk (conference and education slide archive)
why_relevant: Slide archive from BÉT educational and professional conferences; decks from broker analysts and issuer managements often survive here after the event page is retired, giving a retrievable record of what was said at investor events.

source_name: Budapesti Értéktőzsde YouTube channel (event recordings/webcasts)
why_relevant: BÉT states that its most-watched YouTube content is educational and professional-conference material — i.e. investor-event recordings live here. Video/auto-caption transcripts capture management and analyst statements absent from written decks. URL handle is inferred from the channel's existence as described on bet.hu and is NOT verified; treat as a lead to resolve.

source_name: Equilor Befektetési Zrt. – Hírek, elemzések
why_relevant: Independent Hungarian brokerage (BÉT and Warsaw exchange member) that formally covers MBH Bank with published 12-month target prices; its calls are filed to the exchange by the issuer, making Equilor a named, trackable actor in the HU bank sell-side map.

source_name: MBH Bank Nyrt. – Befektetői kapcsolatok / Tőzsdei gyorsjelentés és befektetői prezentáció (incl. Investor Day decks)
source_subtype: issuer IR page with investor-day and flash-report PDFs
why_relevant: Hungary's second listed bank runs its own institutional investor events ('Intézményi befektetői találkozó' / Investor Day, e.g. 1 Oct 2025) and posts the decks alongside quarterly flash reports. Investor-day decks routinely disclose strategy and targets ahead of the annual report.
